topic: evaluation of calibrated abstention, evidence completeness, and omission for free-form multi-source generation under temporal and distributional change

gaps.description: No admitted study validates one end-to-end evaluation scheme that jointly measures claim correctness, evidence attribution correctness, citation or evidence completeness, temporal or current-state correctness, omission, calibrated uncertainty, and abstention while preserving separate denominators for those dimensions. The corpus validates individual components and smaller combinations.
gaps.suggested_search_query: "evaluation framework" factuality attribution "evidence completeness" temporal correctness omission uncertainty abstention "free-form generation"
gaps.resolution_notes: Round 2 added report-level omission, factual completeness, temporal-evidence validity, selective-generation, and judge-validation work, but no admitted paper integrates all required dimensions into one validated evaluation scheme with dimension-specific denominators. Evidence includes arXiv:2509.26184, arXiv:2512.17776, arXiv:2607.19322, arXiv:2608.22483, and DOI 10.1109/ACCESS.2026.3679691.

gaps.description: The corpus contains no direct evaluation on private workplace email or Teams-style communication with realistic revisions, quoted history, conflicting updates, delayed or out-of-order arrival, versioned attachments, and permission-constrained evidence. Target-domain fixtures and gold data remain an engineering validation gap.
gaps.resolution_notes: Resolve by constructing a target-domain benchmark or fixture suite from permission-safe synthetic, de-identified, or appropriately governed workplace communication. The suite should explicitly model revisions, quoted-history duplication, conflicting updates, delayed and out-of-order arrival, versioned attachments, access-control boundaries, supersession, and current-state gold labels. Then benchmark the evaluation pipeline against these fixtures with reproducible expected outputs and failure cases. Adjacent literature can inform fixture design, but direct target-domain validation is project-specific.

gaps.description: Calibration and selective prediction for unconstrained free-form generation were insufficiently answered in the previous corpus because earlier calibration work excluded free-form abstractive QA and evidence-sufficiency work measured behavioral abstention in more controlled conditions.
gaps.resolution_notes: Resolved in round 2 by papers directly addressing selective prediction or calibrated abstention for free-form or structured generation: arXiv:2307.09254, arXiv:2604.12046, arXiv:2605.01749, and arXiv:2606.29054. Together they establish that direct selective-generation methods exist, including entailment-based risk control, long-form claim-level factuality-recall trade-offs, selective commitment during generation, and conformal risk-control analyses. Continuing non-stationary calibration is not treated as resolved here and remains separately tracked as gap-8.

gaps.description: The corpus does not establish a general evidence-completeness method that jointly handles compound claims, partially supportive evidence, multiple complementary sources, and temporally versioned evidence. Separate studies cover subsets of these conditions.
gaps.suggested_search_query: "evidence completeness" "compound claims" "partial support" multi-source temporal versioned evidence attribution evaluation
gaps.resolution_notes: Minimal evidence groups, complex-attribution benchmarks, multi-source RAG evaluation, and temporal-evidence metrics cover important subsets, but no admitted study jointly evaluates all four required cases: compound claims, partial support, complementary multi-source support, and temporally versioned evidence. Relevant partial evidence includes arXiv:2404.15588, arXiv:2508.20867, DOI 10.1109/ACCESS.2026.3679691, and DOI 10.18653/v1/2025.acl-long.837.

gaps.description: Report-level omission now has stronger benchmark coverage, but the corpus still does not establish omission detection for evolving workplace work items, due information, superseded facts, or decision-relevant state across time.
gaps.suggested_search_query: "omission detection" temporal summarization evolving state superseded information "decision-relevant" longitudinal workplace
gaps.resolution_notes: Round 2 materially strengthens generic report-level omission and coverage evidence through arXiv:2508.20867, arXiv:2509.26184, arXiv:2512.17776, and arXiv:2607.19322. However, none establishes an evaluation method for longitudinal omission of evolving work-item state, deadlines or due information, superseded facts, and other decision-relevant temporal state in workplace communication.

gaps.description: A target-domain human-review protocol remains an engineering gap: representative or risk-stratified sampling, minimum human-review volume, multi-rater adjudication, confusion matrices, abstention treatment, coverage reporting, and validation of any LLM-assisted judge against independent human judgments remain project-specific choices.
gaps.resolution_notes: Resolve by specifying and preregistering a project-level review protocol: define representative and risk-stratified sampling strata; set review-volume targets using desired confidence or error-detection sensitivity; use independent multi-rater annotation with an adjudication process; report per-class confusion matrices and inter-rater agreement; treat abstentions as an explicit outcome rather than silently dropping them; report selective coverage alongside conditional quality; and validate any LLM-assisted evaluator on a held-out independently human-rated sample before using it operationally. The literature supplies relevant methods, but the final protocol and thresholds require target-domain engineering validation.

gaps.description: The corpus demonstrates evaluator optimization effects and directional judge bias but does not provide a project-specific procedure for preventing acceptance criteria from being overfit to the same automatic evaluator used during development. Independent holdouts, evaluator separation, and regression checks remain an engineering validation problem.
gaps.resolution_notes: Resolve by separating development and acceptance evaluators, freezing acceptance prompts and thresholds before final testing, maintaining a hidden human-verified holdout set, preventing tuning against acceptance-set outputs, periodically rotating or auditing automatic judges, tracking judge-specific regressions, and requiring independent human confirmation for material acceptance-boundary changes. Evaluator-gaming and directional-bias findings motivate these controls, but their concrete implementation is project-specific.

gaps.description: Calibration under continuing temporal or distributional change remains open for non-stationary free-form communication streams. The corpus supplies long-run adaptive coverage results, cross-domain calibration studies, benchmark-aging evidence, and structured-generation risk-control results, but not one validated selective-prediction method for continuously changing workplace communication.
gaps.suggested_search_query: "selective prediction" non-stationary stream "free-form generation" temporal distribution shift calibration abstention
gaps.resolution_notes: Adaptive conformal inference, cross-domain linguistic calibration, benchmark-aging studies, and structured-generation risk-control results address constituent pieces, but no admitted paper validates calibrated selective prediction on a continuing non-stationary workplace communication stream. Relevant partial evidence includes arXiv:2106.00170, arXiv:2404.00474, arXiv:2510.07238, arXiv:2606.29054, and DOI 10.1162/tacl_a_00407.

convergence.next_round_topic: Integrated evaluation of evidence completeness and omission for temporally evolving multi-source free-form generation, with calibrated selective prediction under non-stationary distribution shift
